title: The first supplementary law of quadratic reciprocity, non-residue half, over the constructed integers
statement: The non-residue half of the first supplementary law of quadratic reciprocity. For a modulus p = 2m+1 satisfying this kernel's PrimeCond, with m ODD -- equivalently p congruent to 3 modulo 4 -- the integer -1 is NOT a quadratic residue modulo p, where `Int.IsQuadraticResidue p a` is this prelude's own definition, the existence of an x with x*x congruent to a modulo p. Nothing here is imported or axiomatised: the modulus is this kernel's constructed natural, the congruence is `Int.ModEq` over the constructed integers, and `Kernel::axiom_footprint` for this declaration is EMPTY. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM. The full law is a biconditional -- -1 is a residue mod p exactly when p is congruent to 1 modulo 4 -- and only the non-residue direction is proved here. The other direction needs a WITNESS, and the Euler-criterion route to one requires the CONVERSE of Euler's criterion (a^((p-1)/2) congruent to 1 implies a is a residue), which needs a primitive root or a root-counting argument over a polynomial ring this kernel has no List/Finset to state; `int_prelude/qr_criterion.rs`'s module doc records that gap and this theorem does not close it. So do not read this fact as deciding -1's residue-hood; it decides it in one direction only. Primality is load-bearing and is not discharged: it is what Euler's criterion needs. `Nat.Odd m` is load-bearing too and the theorem is FALSE without it -- at even m the conclusion is the opposite one (mod 5, -1 is a residue, witness 2).

formal.statement: theorem Int.firstSupplementaryLawNotResidue : ((x0 : AxNat) -> ((x1 : And (AxNat.le (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0))) (((x1 : AxNat) -> ((x2 : AxNat.dvd x1 (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0))) -> Or (Eq.{1} AxNat x1 (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) (Eq.{1} AxNat x1 (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0))))))) -> ((x2 : AxNat.Odd x0) -> Not (Int.is_quadratic_residue (Int.ofNat (AxNat.succ (AxNat.mul (AxNat.succ (AxNat.succ AxNat.zero)) x0))) (Int.neg Int.one)))))

No field was hand-transcribed and no prose was authored. `title`, `statement` and `notes` were then REPLACED by hand (lane first-supplementary-law, ADR-1230); every other field is the generator's output unmodified.

notes: Route (`int_prelude/first_supplementary.rs`, ADR-1230). The blocker was NOT the converse of Euler's criterion. It was that every quadratic-residue theorem in `qr_criterion.rs` is stated over a NATURAL representative `ofNat aa` with 0 < aa < pp, and -1 is not a natural. So `Int.euler_criterion_neg_one_imp_not_residue` is applied at aa := 2*m -- -1's canonical representative mod p = 2m+1 -- and the conclusion transported back to -1 along `Int.isQuadraticResidue_of_modEq` (F:int-isquadraticresidue-of-modeq), a lemma nobody had written: quadratic-residue-hood respects ModEq in its second argument, with the witness unchanged. THE HYPOTHESIS IS `Nat.Odd m`, NOT `p mod 4 = 3`, AND THAT IS LOAD-BEARING. `Nat.div` and `Nat.mod` are stuck at symbolic arguments, so a mod-4 hypothesis would have to be unpacked back into p's constructor shape before anything could use it. `Nat.Odd`'s witness runs the other way: it EMITS the equation m = succ (k+k), from which Le 1 m is `succ_le_succ (zero_le (k+k))` transported backwards, with no arithmetic and no division. This is the same lever that closed the second supplementary law (ADR-1150). THE m = 0 BOUNDARY. Two of the Euler detector's side conditions -- 0 < 2*m and 2 < p -- are false at m = 0 (the modulus would be 1), so both take Le 1 m from oddness rather than from primality. The third, 2*m < p, is `Nat.lt_succ_self` and holds at m = 0 as well; an earlier draft of this note claimed all three fail and the C4 row of docs/research/09-decisions/adr-1230-first-supplementary-checks.py refuted it. p - 1 = m + m needs no bridging step at all: `Nat.sub` recurses on its second argument, so sub (succ (mul 2 m)) 1 iota-reduces to mul 2 m and `two_mul_eq_add_self` is accepted at the stated type by def_eq. NOTHING WAS RE-DERIVED: `two_mul_eq_add_self` and `odd_predicate` were private in `second_supplementary.rs` and `int_exists_intro` private in `euler.rs`; all three were exposed rather than rebuilt. MUTATION MEASUREMENT, both columns. Eight mutations, all caught, none surviving. Four the KERNEL rejected (the sign lemma swapped odd->even; the conclusion -1 -> +1; the detector applied at aa := m; `one_le_of_odd` weakened to 0 <= m). Four only the TEST caught, including the one that matters: concluding at ofNat (2m) instead of -1 produces a statement the kernel admits and which is TRUE, but which is not this law. No axiom footprint, prelude build or inventory check can see that difference. WHAT THE CONTROLS DO NOT CATCH: the test never constructs a PrimeCond proof, so hypothesis satisfiability is evidence from outside the kernel (the numeric script's C1/C2 rows, over the 94 odd primes below 500). CONCRETE CHECK, disjoint from the symbolic one: `first_supplementary_law_refuses_neg_one_exactly_when_the_half_is_odd` (int_prelude_tests.rs) scans [0,p) for x with x*x + 1 = 0 mod p at p = 3, 5, 7, confirming -1 is a non-residue at the two odd-m rows and a residue at the even-m row -- so the parity hypothesis is what decides the conclusion. It then applies the theorem at a genuinely FREE m and compares the inferred type against an independently rebuilt statement, with a control that is refutable IN-KERNEL rather than merely different: the same statement at +1 contradicts `Int.is_quadratic_residue_one`, which holds for every modulus.
